clue.text: Hold weapons tight and refuse to give in

definitions.meaning: the literal reading: keep a firm grip on your firearms
the idiom for holding firm to your position under pressure

explanation.surface: A soldier grips the rifle and will not surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means standing firm on an opinion, from soldiers who kept firing rather than surrender.

clue.text: A youngster held captive by evil Crusade warrior

indicators.note: something held captive is enclosed by its captor, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: evil, wickedness, is sin
a lad is a youngster

explanation.surface: A boy is taken prisoner by a wicked soldier of the Crusades.
explanation.definitionFit: Saladin was the Muslim sultan who fought against the Crusaders in the twelfth century.

clue.text: Old American's behind bars, presumably

definitions.meaning: a member of the ancient Peruvian empire
in the can, slang for in prison

explanation.surface: An ancient American is presumably locked up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the two definitions; read the second as IN CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were the pre-Columbian people of Peru, an old American civilisation; 'can' is slang for jail.

clue.text: Artist preserved, they say, in heaven

indicators.note: signals that the word for preserved is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: food preserved in tins is canned
taken as written
the sky, the heavens

explanation.surface: A painter is kept, people say, in paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: CANNED, said aloud, gives the sound KAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassily Kandinsky was a Russian painter, a pioneer of abstract art.

clue.text: It may get very hot in Slovenia

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the letters of the country's name

explanation.surface: Something gets scorching in the Balkan country of Slovenia.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven is a cooking chamber that heats up to high temperatures.

clue.text: Ignorant individual flipped copper coin outside

indicators.note: flipped means turned over, so the copper coin's name is read backwards

parts.note: the sen was a small copper coin of Japan and elsewhere in Asia

indicators.note: the coin's letters go outside, around the other piece

parts.note: a cent is a coin
I, Roman one, stands for a single individual

explanation.surface: Someone clueless tosses a copper coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Nescient is a formal word meaning lacking knowledge, from Latin nescire, not to know.

clue.text: Young herring: you'll need twenty-four hours to catch a pair

indicators.note: to catch something is to enclose it, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: Saturday, abbreviated Sat, is a day of twenty-four hours

explanation.surface: A fishing tip: allow a full day to land two small fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprat is a small fish of the herring family, often eaten young.

clue.text: Lack of interest in a foreign business

parts.note: un is 'a' in French, a foreign language
a concern is a business or firm

explanation.surface: Someone is indifferent to an overseas company.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconcern is indifference, a lack of care or interest in something.

clue.text: Old singer isn't a performing artist

indicators.note: letters that perform a routine move about, so these are rearranged

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword's usual artist

explanation.surface: An old crooner who claims not to be an entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra was the celebrated twentieth-century American singer.

clue.text: Local folk have terribly nice views beyond lake

indicators.note: the lake comes first and the rest lies past it

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: terribly suggests a mess, so the letters of nice are jumbled

parts.note: views, as a verb, means sees

explanation.surface: Neighbours enjoy lovely scenery beyond a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges NICE to ICEN. A 'local' is British for a neighbourhood pub, whose keepers are licensees.
explanation.definitionFit: Licensees are publicans licensed to sell drink, the folk who run a local pub.

clue.text: Commanding officer operated external transmitter

indicators.note: the operated piece is external, wrapping round the officer

parts.note: to operate a machine is to run it, past tense ran

explanation.surface: An officer in command ran an outside radio set.
explanation.definitionFit: A racon is a radar beacon, a device that transmits a signal in reply to radar.

clue.text: Really like going round a New Zealand port

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the others, enclosing them

parts.note: to dig something is slang for really liking it

explanation.surface: Being keen on a tour of a harbour in New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: Danzig, now Gdansk in Poland, is a Baltic sea port.

clue.text: About start of trial, daughter is in court, easily recognisable

indicators.note: about means around, so these pieces surround the opening letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the word trial

explanation.surface: As a trial begins, a daughter in the courtroom stands out clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinct means clearly marked out, so plainly recognisable from others.

clue.text: Most agreeable, the Promenade des Anglais?

definitions.meaning: this famous seafront road is a Nice street

explanation.surface: Is the famous seafront walk the loveliest place?
explanation.definitionFit: Nicest is the superlative of nice, pleasant; the Promenade des Anglais is the seafront avenue in Nice.

clue.text: Friar still said to lead special group

indicators.note: this piece leads, coming before the group
the word for still is taken by its sound in non-rhotic speech

parts.note: still means calm, untroubled
an elite is a select or special group

explanation.surface: A monk is reportedly about to head a select band.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech CALM sounds like CARM.
explanation.definitionFit: A Carmelite is a friar of the Order of Our Lady of Mount Carmel.

clue.text: Where film is not shown to the public?

definitions.meaning: photographic film is loaded in a camera
the legal phrase for a hearing held in private

explanation.surface: A film kept away from the public eye.
explanation.definitionFit: In camera is the legal Latin for in private chambers, closed to the public.

clue.text: Asking for donation to charity? Charming

definitions.meaning: making an appeal, as a charity does for funds

explanation.surface: Seeking gifts for a good cause is delightful.
explanation.definitionFit: Appealing means both making an appeal for money and attractive or engaging.

clue.text: Saucy past surprisingly ignored by a queen?

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letter a is dropped from the pool, being ignored

explanation.surface: A cheeky history unexpectedly passed over by a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored by' is the signal to drop the A from the pool. In cat breeding a queen is a female cat, which is why the definition carries a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen is a female cat, and a pussycat is a cat, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Take away and execute

definitions.meaning: food bought to eat elsewhere, the American term

explanation.surface: Remove someone and put them to death.
explanation.definitionFit: Carry-out is the American and Scottish word for takeaway food; to carry out a task is to execute it.

clue.text: Film sequence showing what some flowers do at dusk

definitions.meaning: a shot taken from very near the subject

definitions.text: what some flowers do at dusk
definitions.meaning: some flowers shut their petals in the evening

explanation.surface: A movie shot showing blooms folding at evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-up is a tightly framed film shot; many flowers close up at nightfall.

clue.text: Musical instrument with tuning peg fixed on the outside

indicators.note: the fixed piece is outside, surrounding the peg

parts.note: fixed, made firm, is set
a pin is a peg round which a string is wound for tuning

explanation.surface: A keyboard instrument has a tuning peg fitted outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinet is a small harpsichord, a keyboard instrument with plucked strings.

clue.text: Form of transport precedes royal coach

indicators.note: the transport comes before the royal piece

parts.note: a train is a means of transport
ER, Elizabeth Regina, marks the royal queen

explanation.surface: A train goes ahead of the royal carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is a coach, one who trains athletes.

clue.text: Gloomy, as a play's director is?

definitions.meaning: having finished casting, the director is done with the cast

explanation.surface: A dreary director after the auditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcast means covered with cloud, so dull and gloomy.

clue.text: Wild enthusiasm of gangster twins, reportedly

indicators.note: the gangsters' name is taken as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: Ronnie and Reggie Kray were notorious London gangster twins of the 1960s

explanation.surface: The fervour surrounding a pair of notorious criminal brothers, by all accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: The Krays were East End London crime bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: A craze is a passing fad pursued with wild enthusiasm.

clue.text: Queasy feeling experienced originally in foreign sauna

indicators.note: foreign suggests something altered, so the letters are rearranged
takes the first letter of experienced

explanation.surface: Someone felt sick in an overseas steam bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges E and SAUNA together; 'in' links them.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is the feeling of sickness in the stomach, queasiness.

clue.text: Satirist set riddle about wife

indicators.note: about means around, so the riddle's synonym surrounds the wife

parts.note: to riddle is to pass through a sieve, to sift

explanation.surface: A satirical writer poses a puzzle concerning his spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift, author of Gulliver's Travels, was the great Irish satirist.

clue.text: One way or the other, it was worth very little in India

definitions.text: it was worth very little in India

indicators.note: the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.words: it was worth very little in India
parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A coin of tiny value in India, whichever way you look.
explanation.definitionFit: The anna was a former Indian coin worth one sixteenth of a rupee.

clue.text: Plant one found in west-facing area of land

indicators.note: the one is found inside the area of land
in an across clue facing west means reading right to left

parts.note: an acre is a measure of land area
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A shrub is discovered in a plot of land facing west.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers.

clue.text: State qualification

explanation.surface: A credential of the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Condition means both a state of being and a stipulation that qualifies an agreement.

clue.text: Compère will welcome anything after end of dreadful play

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the host takes the other pieces inside

parts.note: a compère is the host of a show, a presenter

indicators.note: anything comes after the final letter
takes the last letter of the word dreadful

parts.note: aught is an old word for anything

explanation.surface: A host will greet anything after a terrible show.
explanation.definitionFit: Present Laughter is a 1939 comedy play by Noel Coward.
